MODEL DOCUMENTATION

How the model works

Methodology, coefficients, simulated performance, and limitations for the reduced ordinal linear model.

METHOD

Ordinal linear scoring

The model standardizes five numeric inputs, adds the applicable neurological category weight, and combines them with an intercept of 1.7867. The continuous result is rounded to the nearest integer and clipped to 0–4, which maps to stages A–E.

score = 1.7867 + Σ(standardized input × β) + neurological β

DESIGN

Why six inputs?

MAP, cardiac index, lactate, SvO₂, urine output, and neurological assessment retained most of the predictive information in the synthetic dataset. Other variables were excluded when they added little independent signal or largely duplicated stronger predictors.

STANDARDIZED WEIGHTS

A positive coefficient raises the calculated severity score; a negative coefficient lowers it.

LIMITATIONS

Interpret performance cautiously

The reported accuracy measures agreement with labels in synthetic, literature-informed data—not diagnostic performance in real patients. The model does not evaluate treatment response, medication escalation, pH, mechanical support, cardiac arrest, or longitudinal deterioration. It is a research and workflow-development prototype rather than a validated clinical decision instrument.
